entry.title: The Web Can't Afford a JavaScript Runtime Monoculture (6 minute read)
entry.content:
Deno's planned end of runtime development narrows the major server-side JavaScript choices to Node.js, Bun, and Cloudflare's workerd. Historical examples from Internet Explorer and the io.js fork show how independent implementations can prevent stagnation and push features into competing runtimes.

From TLDR Dev · 2026-10-30 · Articles & Tutorials

entry.title: Measuring Soft Navigation Web Vitals (11 minute read)
entry.content:
Sentry's JavaScript SDK v11 measures LCP, CLS, and INP for client-side navigations, exposing slow routes that initial page-load metrics miss. Support currently requires Chromium 151 or later, and the scores should be filtered separately from page loads because their clocks start at different points.

From TLDR Dev · 2026-10-30 · Articles & Tutorials

entry.title: Optimizing the sh*t out of TanStack Start (17 minute read)
entry.content:
A TanStack Start site improved its mobile Lighthouse score from 73 to 100 and reduced LCP from 5.2 seconds to 1.7 seconds by removing unnecessary JavaScript, images, and font data. More complex changes added maintenance without clearly explaining the final score, making basic asset reductions and regression budgets the more useful starting point.

From TLDR Dev · 2026-10-30 · Articles & Tutorials

entry.title: How I Built the Most AI-Pilled Company in the World (18 minute read)
entry.content:
Spawn reports shipping 77,000 substantial changes in 30 days with a ten-person team and $3.1 million in token spending, using permanent agents that own parts of the company. Its approach combines direct production feedback, frequent tests, hourly deployments, and fast recovery, with hard-coded gates for irreversible actions. Humans focus on product taste and ambitious changes that agents rarely propose themselves.

entry.title: Design Systems Should Be Fast by Default (18 minute read)
entry.content:
Benchmarks of large dropdowns and checkbox lists across ten design systems trace slow interactions to repeated layout work, slot handling, and per-checkbox animations. Published Playwright tests enforce timing budgets so shared components can catch performance regressions before they reach every consuming app.

entry.content:

Core-team tools shipped within minutes, while the default Docker image took almost 16 hours and some cloud runtimes took days, showing why teams need to audit the entire update path.

entry.title: How to make postMessage type-safe in under 350 bytes (9 minute read)
entry.content:
typed-channel defines message names and payloads once so TypeScript can check both sides of a worker, iframe, or event-bus boundary. The core plus postMessage transport is 341 bytes with Brotli compression, while a separate request API adds typed replies and cancellation that propagates to the handler.

entry.title: Local-First Means Three Different Things (9 minute read)
entry.content:
Local-first can mean offline capability, fast optimistic interfaces, or user ownership of data, and those promises lead to different architectures. Hologram prioritizes responsive local interfaces and offline support while retaining a server to enforce permissions and business rules.

entry.title: The AI cost of JavaScript frameworks (15 minute read)
entry.content:
A benchmark asks Opus 5.5 to build the same Pokémon app across JavaScript frameworks, then measures cost, time, spec compliance, performance, and accessibility over repeated runs. Hono with htmx, Astro, and Nuxt are among the cheapest in this experiment, but substantial run-to-run variance and a mostly content-focused app limit how broadly the ranking applies.

entry.content:

The prediction shifts the durable sources of lock-in toward contracts, procurement approvals, and agent memory, making portable requirements and decision logs more valuable.

entry.content:

The fix uses one curated timezone list and integration tests that compare both systems, rather than validating against either runtime alone.

entry.content:

It also caps review cycles after one PR bounced between agents more than fifty times overnight.

entry.content:

Constrained decoding raised schema accuracy to 100% for its supported Kimi and DeepSeek models by blocking invalid tokens during generation, though that guarantee does not establish whether a tool call is useful or correct.

entry.content:

Real headings, native lists, and one maintained copy help more than visual formatting, while conversion tools need care because Word comments and tracked changes can disappear during a Markdown round trip.

The model was restored in September after remediation, and the October disclosure explains how a rejected request could still decode against stale cache pages.

entry.content:

The result is 63% smaller than compressing the original floats, while typed arrays and an animation loop that sleeps when idle reduce rendering work.

Engineers approve every fix, while 22 evaluation cases test real incidents and past mistakes.

Staff need role-specific training, time to experiment, and a reason to share in productivity gains without fearing punishment for mistakes. Shadow AI can reveal gaps in official tools that blanket restrictions only push out of sight.

From TLDR Dev · 2026-10-23 · Miscellaneous

entry.title: What the heck is the Public Suffix List? (21 minute read)
entry.content:
The Public Suffix List records the boundaries browsers and password managers need to distinguish independently controlled sites on shared domains. Codex emerged from parallel efforts in research automation and coding-product design, followed by a pivot after the initial cloud product struggled to find traction. The account traces the shift toward local workflows, a shared Rust agent core, and models trained for interactive work in messy codebases.
